content:
Hi everyone,

I wonder what is consensus here about using AI to formally verify software with Lean4?
As a total verification-newbie I used Fable to formally verify RAFT cluster consensus layer using Lean4: https://github.com/PeterKnego/ultima_cluster/blob/main/docs/VERIFICATION.md

I personally believe it's the future of software engineering. However it's still expensive and limited to a specific class of very well defined and stable software. The reality of software engineering in real world scenarios is that software is extremely volatile.
It's very likely to get much better in the next 10 years though

Peter Knego said:

As a total verification-newbie I used Fable to formally verify RAFT cluster consensus layer using Lean4

You should check out section 7.2 of the loom paper: https://verse-lab.org/papers/loom-popl26.pdf

They implement the NOPaxos protocol in Veil, which is a Lean metaprogramming framework specifically designed for verifying network protocols. It seems perfect for this RAFT application.

@Jack McCarthy
Than you for the link - will check it out.
I did try Veil after Lean4 successfully found five bugs, so it makes sense Veil did not find any new bugs: https://github.com/PeterKnego/ultima_cluster/tree/main/proofs-veil

I'm doing something similar, it's very useful for checking algorithms, catches so many bugs and you can keep your normal programming language if AI reimplements a function in lean4 and check one implementation against the other using differential testing

It's also useful to use SMT for some other cases (for example Z3)

@Peter Knego Also, can you clarify the relationship between the rust crates in your project and the Lean modules? Your VERIFICATION.md file specifically says that you did not perform rust-to-lean extraction, so I assume the Lean Uc2Model folder is just an AI translation of the Rust code. Is it possible to use a tool like Aeneas here? https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas

@Jack McCarthy
Correct in ultima_cluster Lean model was AI-derived from code and then verified.
Afaik, Aeneas is not possible to use on ultima_cluster because it uses unsafe in a few places, which Aeneas does not support.

However, I did use Aenas in ultima_db: https://github.com/PeterKnego/ultima_db/blob/main/formal/WRITEUP.md

Do you think it would be possible to remove the unsafe Rust code and get something that works in the subset of Rust covered by Aeneas? Or is this something that is intrinsic to the RAFT protocol?

I just think that a Lean formalization is only as trustworthy as the underlying model. If the Rust->Lean translation is done by AI, then you're still relying on nondeterministic LLMs to write the model/spec which some might argue defeats the point of doing formal methods (although you said that formalization helped you find bugs in the protocol, which is perhaps of independent value).
